headings.title: SMTO-LLM-0102 — SMTO couldn't reach your image model, and Main can't read images

html:
SMTO-LLM-0102 — SMTO couldn't reach your image model, and Main can't read images

GUID: bf92bd1b-bc56-5f2d-b7aa-54d0f9f02d9f
Slug: vision-route-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: vision

What happened

  • The model set up to read images (Vision) couldn't be used, and your Main model, which SMTO tries next, can't read pictures. So the image wasn't looked at.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the program running your Vision model is switched on and reachable. If someone else runs it, ask them to check and restart it. The Vision connection failed first; Main was only the backup and can't take over picture reading.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, check the Vision card's Endpoint and Model, and select Check saved model. It confirms SMTO can reach the Vision model again.
  3. If the Vision model can't be fixed soon, enter a different image-capable model on the Vision card, select Save Vision, and start a new task. New tasks use the saved Vision settings; a task already running keeps its original ones.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model on the Vision card passes, and SMTO's reply describes your image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the Vision model. Until this works, don't rely on any SMTO answer about that image; it wasn't looked at.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The configured Vision route failed (for example a connection or provider error) and the permitted fallback to Main was refused because Main does not advertise image input.

What this means

  • The configured Vision route failed and its permitted fallback reached Main without advertised image input. The fallback capability error does not erase the original connection failure. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The configured Vision route failed and its permitted fallback reached Main without advertised image input. The fallback capability error does not erase the original connection failure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Restore the Vision endpoint: check its process or managed instance, base URL, served model and multimodal projector, then run Check saved model on the Vision role. Alternatively configure a different image-capable Vision connection for new tasks; Main is a valid fallback only when it advertises image input.
  • Check or restart the selected Vision instance and verify its connection, model and projector. Continue with the same recovered endpoint, or configure a new task for a different image-capable connection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected Vision endpoint is ready and returns a substantive observation for the retained authorized source.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
